r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: Scope and mechanics match the handoff (all six templates swept per CENSUS.md, 3 edited, edits match the pre-ruling shape). But the handoff's second, named deliverable -- "fix the gate that cannot fail (#562)" -- is not reliably fixed. I scanned every implementer-result evidence record recorded in this repo's .agent-work/ tree (119 records across 40+ real Commander runs, archived and live) for the payload.status field the new match={"status":"complete"} check requires: only 28/119 (24%) carry status=="complete" exactly. 41/119 use a "verdict" field instead (more common than "status" in this corpus), 36/119 carry neither field, 11/119 use a bespoke schema (gate_id/red_exit/green_exit), and 3 more carry status in the wrong case ("COMPLETE"). checklist_engine.py:853-855 does exact case-sensitive dict equality on payload, so all of these except the 28 would fail the new check. The fix does not convert a check that cannot fail into one that reliably passes for legitimate work -- it converts it into one that passes for a minority convention and fails the plurality convention ("verdict") along with every Commander that attaches no such field. See r4a for the full evidence and verdict on whether this blocks the change.

r4a-satisfiable.title: Is g1-implement.c1 now satisfiable by a real Commander?
r4a-satisfiable.imperative: THE DECISIVE QUESTION. The #562 fix adds match={"status":"complete"} to the implementer-result artifact check. Nothing in the repo tells a Commander to attach a `status` field when it integrates an IMPLEMENTER_RESULT — the implementer itself said so in its own Assumptions section. Search the archived spines under .agent-work/ (and any tracked history you can reach) for every implementer-result evidence record actually attached by a real run, and report the exact payload fields found. If real runs attach no `status`, this change turns a check that cannot fail into a check that cannot pass, and every Commander implement gate is permanently blocked. That is a BLOCK. Say which it is, with the payloads you found.
r4a-satisfiable.finding: BLOCK. I scanned every execute.json under .agent-work/ (archived and live, this worktree) for evidence entries with type=="implementer-result" and inspected their payload fields with a script, not by sampling: 119 records found across 40+ real Commander runs spanning 2026-07-08 through 2026-08-10. Breakdown of the completion-state field actually used: 31 records use "status" (28 exactly =="complete", 3 wrong-case e.g. "COMPLETE"), 41 records use "verdict" instead (values like "complete", "COMPLETE", "COMPLETE -- no unresolved blockers", or free text like "WIN - the done-condition is met..."), 36 records carry NEITHER field (payloads like {path, summary}, {path, blockers, crew}, {path, session, verified, note}), and 11 records use a wholly different bespoke schema ({gate_id, red_exit, green_exit}) from a hand-built execute.json. checklist_engine.py:853-855 does exact case-sensitive dict equality (`ev["payload"].get(k) == v`), confirmed by reading the source. So only 28/119 (24%) of this repo's own real implementer-result evidence history would satisfy the new match={"status":"complete"}; the plurality convention in actual use is "verdict" (41, more common than "status"'s 31), which the fix does not recognize at all. This is not "nothing tells a Commander to attach a status field" (a documentation gap) -- it is "Commanders in this repo's own history have never converged on one field name," so the fix does not convert a check that cannot fail into one that reliably passes for legitimate completed work. It converts it into one that blocks 76% of the historical shapes outright, including the single MOST COMMON shape ("verdict"). Every future Commander implement gate that follows the more common precedent, or any precedent other than exact status=="complete", is now permanently blocked at g1-implement.c1 -- reproducing #562's own defect with the sign flipped, exactly as the review handoff warned. Full per-file payload dump available on request; representative examples: commander-424 (status:"complete"), commander-f2 (verdict:"complete"), r418-460/issue-467-trip-semantics (neither field), issue-418-iterative-planning (gate_id/red_exit/green_exit schema).

r4b-init-check-side-effect.title: Does the Admiral init check refuse a healthy run?
r4b-init-check-side-effect.imperative: ADMIRAL_SPINE.init.c1 now RUNS init_work_area.py as its check, so the check mutates the repo every time the engine evaluates it, including on re-evaluation after the work area already exists. Confirm it is idempotent. Then confirm the `test -f .agent-work/<work-id>/ADMIRAL_LOG.md` half resolves correctly when the Admiral runs inside a git worktree — scripts/agent_work_root.py::durable_root deliberately relocates .agent-work depending on whether an epic lease is held, and this check hardcodes a relative path. Drive a real Admiral spine through init in a worktree and say what happened.
r4b-init-check-side-effect.finding: Not a defect, tested empirically. Idempotency: init_work_area.py's init_work_area() does `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` per subdir and never touches an existing file -- I ran the exact check command (`python ./scripts/init_work_area.py demo-r4b && test -f .agent-work/demo-r4b/ADMIRAL_LOG.md`) twice directly after ADMIRAL_LOG.md existed; both exits were 0 and the log file's md5sum was unchanged, confirming no mutation on re-evaluation. Worktree path resolution: I built a real linked worktree (`git worktree add --detach /tmp/r4b-worktree <snapshot>`), instantiated a scratch ADMIRAL_SPINE.template.json spine there, and drove init.c1 through the real engine end to end (claim -> start -> advance refuses on missing ADMIRAL_LOG.md -> create it -> advance succeeds, "init -> complete" exit 0). The work area landed at the worktree's own .agent-work/demo-r4b/, confirmed absent from the main checkout's .agent-work/. On the durable_root concern specifically: I read scripts/agent_work_root.py and confirmed init_work_area.py never imports or calls durable_root() -- its --root defaults to "." (cwd) unconditionally. durable_root()'s relocation is scoped, by its own module docstring, to CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md and the episode-store sidecar ledger, not to the general per-work-id .agent-work/<work-id>/ tree. The downstream consumer of ADMIRAL_LOG.md (verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py's _work_area(), used at the already-shipped execute.c3) also resolves via a bare `Path.cwd().joinpath(".agent-work", *segments)` -- not durable_root() either. So init.c1's hardcoded relative path is internally consistent with every other reader of ADMIRAL_LOG.md in this pipeline; the concern raised in the handoff does not materialize because durable_root was never in this check's code path to begin with. The existing, documented, out-of-scope fragility (#341: command checks depend on the launcher's cwd generally) is unchanged by this diff and not introduced by it.

But the sweep also surfaced a real miscount the census's "19 already fine, no action" verdict did not catch: REVIEW_SURVEY.template.json's r6-fowler.c1 check command ships with a literal `<fowler-pass-record-path>` placeholder that resolve_spine's token set (work-id/role-skill-dir/role-session-id/repo-root only) cannot resolve -- unlike the item's own claim that it resolves "exactly like <work-id>." r4d-explorer-weakening.title: Was weakening EXPLORER_SPINE.init.c1's statement the right call?
r4d-explorer-weakening.imperative: The implementer weakened the statement instead of strengthening the check, reasoning that spine.json's existence is a bootstrap invariant. Test that reasoning: can the engine reach this gate with no spine.json? If the claim is right the weakening is right; if it is wrong, the honest fix was to constrain the check.
r4d-explorer-weakening.finding: Tested the implementer's bootstrap-invariant argument directly rather than accepting it. Ran `python scripts/checklist_engine.py --file /tmp/nonexistent-spine.json advance init --mechanical --session-id demo` (and `current`, and `claim`) against a spine.json that does not exist: every verb raises an unhandled FileNotFoundError at `load()` (checklist_engine.py:175, called from main() before any verb-specific logic runs) -- confirmed for three different verbs, all failing identically at the same load step. This means the engine cannot evaluate ANY postcondition, including init.c1, without spine.json already existing on disk; there is no code path where the engine is "running this advance" against a file that isn't there. So EXPLORER_SPINE.init.c1's bare command check (`init_work_area.py <work-id>`, no --spine/--skill-dir) can never be evaluated while its statement's dropped clause ("spine.json materialized") is false -- the property holds by construction before the check ever runs, making a `test -f spine.json` addition to the check tautological, not a strengthening. Weakening the statement to match what the check actually tests (rather than adding a check that cannot fail) was the correct call, consistent with the already-shipped g1-review.c1 pattern this diff cites as precedent.

The decisive item (r4a) is empirically confirmed: I scanned all 119 real implementer-result evidence records recorded anywhere under .agent-work/ in this repo's history and found only 24% (28/119) carry payload.status=="complete", the exact literal the new match={"status":"complete"} check requires (checklist_engine.py does case-sensitive dict equality). This is the same defect with the sign flipped, exactly as the review handoff warned, and it would block real Commander implement gates repo-wide once this template ships. r4-quality and r4c independently corroborate the same root cause (a guessed, unenforced field convention) and a related, previously-uncaught census miscount (REVIEW_SURVEY.template.json's r6-fowler.c1 ships with an unresolvable placeholder), respectively. Everything else checked out clean: scope and hard no-gos respected (r2), full suite reproduced exactly as claimed -- 2532 passed, 1 skipped, 1102 subtests (r3), no architecture to reconcile (r5), Fowler pass clean modulo one flagged primitive-obsession smell tracing to the same root cause (r6), the ADMIRAL_SPINE.init.c1 check is idempotent and resolves correctly in a real linked worktree with no durable_root mismatch (r4b), and the EXPLORER_SPINE.init.c1 statement-weakening argument holds up under direct testing -- the engine provably cannot evaluate that gate without spine.json already existing (r4d). The fix is fixable: either constrain the check to whatever field convention the repo actually documents and enforces (which does not exist yet -- see the flagged triage candidate and the implementer's own Out-of-scope note), or revert to a presence-only check honestly matching g1-review.c1's pattern until that convention is written down and enforced.
